problem: Training and studying RL agents for human-aware social navigation with multiple perceptual modalities lacks an open, modular, multi-modal simulation and training framework; existing setups do not easily allow comparing features, encodings, fusion and RL algorithms.
motivation: Social interaction is inherently multi-modal (cameras, LIDAR, ultrasound, microphones), and applications include social robotics, VR and games. A common open framework allows systematic study of perceptual features, their encoding and fusion, and agent types for social navigation.
key_idea: OpenSocInt is an open-source, modular package (simulator, environment, agent) with a 2D social-force-based pedestrian simulator, several sensing modalities (closest obstacle, LIDAR raycast, local egocentric occupancy grid), a shared multi-modal latent encoder and four deep RL agents (SAC, TD3, DDPG, A2C).
insight: Across modalities, all converge to similar asymptotic performance, but differ early in training and in variance: simple features learn faster, LEOG gives lower variance with more data, and fusing RayCast+LEOG gives better low-data performance and more stable training (fewer sporadic truncation spikes). Pre-training the LEOG encoder helps early training and reduces variance vs. training from scratch. The RL algorithm matters a lot: SAC works best, while A2C and DDPG collapse into a people-avoiding policy (truncation rate goes to 1) and TD3 behaves nearly randomly.
method: Simulator module: tracks the agent, static/dynamic obstacles and goal; pedestrians move by a weighted sum of a goal force and a social (repulsion) force. The repulsion ignores the agent, since the agent learned to exploit it to push humans away.

Environment module: mediates between agent and simulator and converts the state into observations: closest-obstacle coordinates (Cartesian/polar), LIDAR raycast (e.g. 360 values), or local egocentric occupancy grid (e.g. 6x6 m at 0.1 m gives 60x60), plus the relative goal position and reward.

Agent module: modality-specific encoders (CNN+FC for LEOG, FC for the others, RBF layer for low-dimensional inputs), concatenation-based fusion into a shared latent space, on which TD3, DDPG, A2C and SAC agents are built.
LEOG encoder pre-training: the encoder is pre-trained on data collected with a random policy (online or from an existing dataset), then frozen, fine-tuned, or trained from scratch.
Reward: r_int = step penalty + goal-direction term + social-repulsion term; terminal reward for goal (+500) or collision (-500); weights w_step=-5, w_goal-d=10, w_social=-100.

setting.backbone: Small CNN/MLP encoders with RBF layers, trained from scratch with SAC / TD3 / DDPG / A2C
setting.training_data: Online RL interaction in the simulator, 700 training episodes; the LEOG encoder is optionally pre-trained on random-policy data (scale not given)
setting.observation: Simulated closest-obstacle polar coordinates, 360-ray LIDAR, and/or local egocentric occupancy grid, plus the relative goal position
setting.action_space: Continuous agent motion (actor-critic RL; exact parametrization not detailed)

numbers_note: Results are only shown as training curves in figures (success/collision/truncated rates, mean/std); no numeric tables or values are printed.
results: All three LEOG encoder strategies and all three modalities converge to excellent performance, differing in variance and early learning. Multi-modal LEOG+RayCast fusion gives more stable, more data-efficient learning. Among RL paradigms, SAC is best (rapid drop in collisions, almost no truncations), followed by TD3, DDPG and A2C.
limitations: Only a simple 2D simulator with social-force pedestrians; no rich social cues yet and only navigation is evaluated
Results are qualitative curves without quantitative tables, no comparison to other social navigation benchmarks or real-robot tests
